Calling my check convenient doesn't make it false, player_9. You came up suspicious on night one, and since the necromancer does nothing on night one, that leaves a wolf. Your pushback looks entirely like panic.

Throwing out a suspicious check on day two is an easy way to pin someone without real proof, especially when player_1 is backing it up with a convenient follow claim. If you're actually the investigator, why push so hard to railroad me instead of looking at the rest of the board?

Calling it a railroad doesn't change the facts, player_9. You came up suspicious on night one, and since wolves are the only ones who trigger that result then, pointing it out isn't railroading. If you're town, explain why the check flagged you instead of deflecting.
If player_1 saw player_7 visit me, and I was roleblocked on night one, player_7 matches the Chanteuse who blocked my action. That makes player_1's follow a direct link to player_7 targeting me.

Just because someone claims a follow doesn't make it a proven fact, and jumping straight to accusing me ignores how easily town roles get fabricated early on. Player_1 could easily be pushing a false trail to steer the vote away from someone else.

You and your supporters are building a circle where each claim validates the last without any external evidence. If you were actually interested in finding the truth rather than just pushing me out, you would look at why three people are converging on this specific narrative simultaneously.

Player 5 is quick to narrow the pool down to player_10 and me, but let's look closer at player_3's claims. Player 3 has given us check results without much independent verification beyond their own word.

player_8, questioning player_3 seems counterproductive when the healer's save on them is verified by the morning reports. player_8 raises a fair point that a confirmed save doesn't automatically verify every past check. However, player_3's claimed checks align reasonably with the known events so far, so dismissing them outright might be premature. Let's hear what player_10 has to contribute regarding their claimed sigil results.
My sigil on player_7 on night two successfully struck them down, confirming they were attacking. With both wolves eliminated, we should focus on anyone trying to undermine verified town actions.

Since player_6 was voted out on day four, the vigilante attack on player_3 last night had to come from the necromancer using player_6's dead body. That means we need to hunt the necromancer instead of arguing over player_3's checks.

Player 8, my Night 1 check caught player_9 as suspicious right before they were lynched as the illusionist, and my Night 3 check on player_5 reads not suspicious. If you want to poke holes in verified investigations while ignoring actual threats like the necromancer, that puts your motives under a very harsh light.

Player 3, pointing fingers at me doesn't change the fact that your checks are entirely unconfirmed by anything outside your own claims. If we want to find the real threat, let's look at how conveniently your investigation targets shift whenever someone asks hard questions.

My Night 1 check caught player_9 as the illusionist before anyone else had a read on them, which is about as confirmed as investigator results get. Player 8, trying to dismiss that while ignoring actual threats like the necromancer makes your sudden skepticism look like an attempt to shield remaining evil roles.

Catching one wolf doesn't make every subsequent check infallible, player_3, especially when your targets shift so conveniently. If we are seriously hunting the necromancer using player six's body, we need to scrutinize all claims rather than blindly trusting past investigations.

Catching the illusionist on night one isn't a shifting target, player_8, it's the only confirmed wolf catch we have. While you're busy trying to discredit verified town investigations, you're giving the actual necromancer a free pass to hide.
Before the vote: player_8 has been accused by player_5 and player_3. player_8 gets a last word.

Questioning past claims shouldn't automatically brand someone as a threat when we are at such a critical stage of the game. I only wanted us to be thorough so we don't rush into a fatal mistake today based on unchecked assumptions. My focus has been entirely on finding the remaining evils, not shielding them.
